panels.title: Hereditary Breast & Ovarian Cancer Panel
panels.description: Genes and variants most often included on clinical hereditary breast and ovarian cancer (HBOC) multi-gene panels, spanning BRCA1/BRCA2 and the other DNA-damage-repair genes tested alongside them.

panels.title: Lynch Syndrome (Hereditary Colorectal & Endometrial Cancer) Panel
panels.description: The mismatch-repair genes screened for Lynch syndrome, the most common inherited cause of colorectal and endometrial cancer.

panels.title: Hereditary Thrombophilia Panel
panels.description: The two variants most frequently tested in an inherited clotting-risk workup: Factor V Leiden and the prothrombin G20210A variant.

panels.title: Core Pharmacogenomics (Drug-Metabolism) Panel
panels.description: A core set of pharmacogenes that influence how common medications are metabolized and dosed, drawn from CPIC/PharmGKB-style clinical pharmacogenomic panels.

panels.title: Familial Hypercholesterolemia Panel
panels.description: The three genes most commonly implicated in familial hypercholesterolemia, an inherited cause of very high LDL cholesterol and early cardiovascular disease.

panels.title: Cystic Fibrosis (CFTR) Panel
panels.description: The CFTR gene and its best-known variants, including F508del, the most common cystic-fibrosis-causing variant.

panels.title: Hereditary Hemochromatosis (HFE) Panel
panels.description: The HFE gene and its two classic variants (C282Y and H63D) associated with hereditary iron-overload disease.

panels.title: Inherited Cardiomyopathy Panel
panels.description: Core genes screened for inherited cardiomyopathies, including hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (MYH7, MYBPC3) and the LMNA-related cardiomyopathies.

panels.title: Parkinson's Disease Genetic Risk Panel
panels.description: The two genes with the strongest, best-replicated links to inherited Parkinson's disease risk, LRRK2 and GBA1, along with their most-studied risk variants.

panels.title: Hemoglobinopathy Panel
panels.description: The hemoglobin genes and variants behind the most common inherited hemoglobin disorders, including the sickle cell variant (HbS) in HBB.
